subject: setting h and v pixels of graphics window

messages.author: 20a7dc1f521322f3
messages.subject: setting h and v pixels of graphics window
parts:
hi everyone

i am wondering about the size of the graphics window. when i make a
plot and use ggsave, then it saves it according to the size of the
window on the screen. but if i graph the same data again later, the
window may not have the exact same number of pixels in both
directions, and the aspect ratio may be different, resulting in a
different looking plot. this can be important, for some graphs are
better tall and other better wide. but the size of the window is just
a random artifact of my screen layout at the time.

how do i force the window on the screen to have a certain number of
pixels in the x- and y- directions? will this ensure that i get the
same graph in the pdf/ps from ggsave? is there a way to force ggsave
to use a certain number of pixels in both axes?

thanks a lot
neal

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: setting h and v pixels of graphics window
parts:
ggsave("image.png", height=X, width=Y)

X and Y are in inches. 

?ggsave()

You can change the dpi if you want something richer.

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: setting h and v pixels of graphics window
parts:
Neal, 

If you want to accurately define the final output size, I'm pretty sure you'll have to hard code it in inches per above. When I started making graphs, I did it the same way, by defining the window size, but that got tedious. If you hard code it, you get the same result every time. Makes more sense in the long run. If you're trying to resize your window a particular way every time it would be a PITA I think. 

Brandon

Hi,

Yes, but the details will depend on your system,

dev.new(width=8,height=3)

opens an 8in x 3in quartz() window for me. It probably does the same
with a windows() window on Windows.

HTH,

baptiste
